Title: Solar System Patterns
Content: Our solar system includes planets, moons, and other space objects that orbit our star, the `text(Sun)`. Movements of `text(Earth)`, the `text(Sun)`, and the `text(Moon)` cause `text(daily)`, `text(monthly)`, and seasonal patterns to occur. Many other stars are visible in the night sky but are located outside our solar system.

The photographs show some stars visible from `text(Earth)`. Alpha Centauri A and B are `text(two)` stars that orbit each other and appear as `text(one)` star in the night sky. Alpha Centauri A is slightly larger than the `text(Sun)` while Alpha Centauri B is slightly smaller than the `text(Sun)`. Another star seen at night, Beta Pavonis, is about `2.3` times larger than the `text(Sun)`. The table shows the distances of these stars from `text(Earth)`.
